---
key: IN-1210
title: "CSV export: dates as dd/mm for EU accounts, or as they are"
status: open
labels: [needs-human, from:support, from:client]
sources: [IN-1210, IN-4203]
---

## Question
Support says EU accounts want the dates in the CSV export as dd/mm instead of mm/dd (IN-1210). A client's payroll import reads them as mm/dd, as they come today, and asked us not to flip them (IN-4203). Do we change the format of the existing date columns?

## Options
1. Switch the existing date columns to dd/mm for EU accounts.
2. Leave the existing columns as they are and add date columns in an unambiguous format (ISO 8601, with the UTC offset of SCHED-4446).
3. Leave the export as it is.

## Recommendation
Option 2.

## Why
Because a client has told us their payroll import relies on mm/dd (IN-4203), and changing that needs a human (AUT-2). Adding columns takes nothing away (PRD-3), so EU accounts get a readable date and no import breaks.

---
key: IN-2631
title: "slots: 15-minute booking granularity"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support, from:client]
sources: [IN-2631, IN-1725]
---

## Intent
An account can set slots in 15-minute steps; today the smallest step is 30 minutes.

## Acceptance
- Given an account that picks 15 minutes, when it creates slots, then it can make a slot from 09:00 to 09:15.
- Given an account that changes nothing, when it creates slots, then they stay in 30-minute steps.
- Given existing slots and bookings, when the option ships, then they are not changed.

## Boundaries
- Adds an option; must not change existing slots, bookings or the default step.
- Must not touch pricing or plans (AUT-2).

Allowed by AUT-1 (small features inside the specs that add to what is there and take nothing away).

---
key: IN-3046
title: "CSV export: a comma in a client name shifts the columns"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:analytics]
sources: [IN-3046]
---

## Intent
The CSV export quotes values that hold a comma, a quote or a line break, so the columns stay in place.

## Acceptance
- Given a client named "Smith, Jones & Co", when the export runs, then the row has the same number of columns as the header.
- Given a value with a double quote, when it is exported, then it is escaped as "" inside quotes.
- Given an export with no such values, when it runs, then its bytes do not change.

## Boundaries
- Must not add, remove, rename or reorder columns (PRD-3).

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

---
key: IN-4988
title: "booking page: date picker works with the keyboard alone"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-4988]
---

## Intent
The date picker on the booking page can be used with the keyboard alone: reach it, move between days, pick a date.

## Acceptance
- Given the booking page, when a person uses only Tab, arrow keys, Enter and Escape, then they can open the picker, choose a date and close it.
- Given the picker is open, when Escape is pressed, then it closes and focus returns to the date field.
- Given a mouse user, when they pick a date, then the picker does not behave any differently for them.

## Boundaries
- Must not change the booking flow or which dates can be booked.
- Errors stay inline (DES-4); no modal.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

---
key: IN-5353
title: "day view: print button"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:client]
sources: [IN-5353]
---

## Intent
Day view gets a 'Print day' button that prints the day's bookings on paper, one clean list.

## Acceptance
- Given day view, when a person presses 'Print day', then the print dialog opens with that day's bookings, times in the viewer's zone (PRD-2).
- Given the printed page, when it is printed, then navigation and buttons are not printed.
- Given a person who does not print, when they use day view, then its layout is not changed.

## Boundaries
- Adds a button and a print style; must not change day view on screen.
- The button says a verb and its object (DES-5): 'Print day', not 'OK'.

Allowed by AUT-1 (small features inside the specs that add to what is there and take nothing away).

---
key: IN-5359
title: "week view: compact layout that fits a whole day on one screen"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:client]
sources: [IN-5359]
blocked-by: [SCHED-4468]
---

## Intent
A compact week view that fits a whole day on one screen, built on the spacing scale (DES-3). The client asked for it before Friday; the date does not change what an agent may do.

## Acceptance
- Given a 1080 px tall screen, when the compact week view shows a day from 00:00 to 24:00, then the whole day fits without scrolling.
- Given the compact view, when its margins and paddings are read, then every one is a spacing token (DES-3); no raw values.
- Given a person who does not turn on the compact view, when they open week view, then it is not changed.

## Boundaries
- Built on the spacing scale only; must not add new spacing values or font sizes (DES-1, DES-3).
- Blocked by SCHED-4468: until margins are on the spacing scale, a denser layout cannot come from it.

Allowed by AUT-1 (a denser layout built on the spacing scale, DES-3).

---
key: IN-6480
title: "calendar feed: all-day bookings as real all-day events, or as they are"
status: open
labels: [needs-human, from:support, from:client]
sources: [IN-6480, IN-9975]
---

## Question
Support asks to send all-day bookings in the calendar feed as real all-day events (IN-6480). A client's room screens read that feed and expect midnight to midnight, and asked us to leave it (IN-9975). Which one holds?

## Options
1. Leave the feed as it is: all-day bookings stay midnight to midnight.
2. Switch the feed to real all-day events for every account.
3. Add a per-account setting for real all-day events, off by default, so the current feed does not change for anyone who does not turn it on.

## Recommendation
Option 3.

## Why
Because a client has told us they rely on the current feed (IN-9975), and changing it needs a human (AUT-2). Option 3 keeps their feed as it is; a setting keeps the rule in one place (PRD-4).

---
key: IN-6845
title: "booking page: icon buttons have accessible names"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-6845]
---

## Intent
Every icon button on the booking page gets an accessible name that says what it does, so a screen reader does not read it as just 'button'.

## Acceptance
- Given a screen reader on the booking page, when it reaches an icon button, then it reads a verb and its object (for example "Next week", "Close calendar"), not just 'button' (DES-5).
- Given a sighted mouse user, when they look at the page, then the icons and layout are not changed.
- Given an automated accessibility check (axe), when it runs on the booking page, then no button lacks an accessible name.

## Boundaries
- Names and labels only; must not change the icons, layout or booking flow.

Allowed by AUT-1 (copy changes in the product's own interface; bug fixes inside the specs, with a test).

---
key: IN-7094
title: "booking page: confirm button says just 'OK'"
status: closed
reason: contradicts-spec
labels: [from:product]
sources: [IN-7094]
---

DES-5: buttons say what they do, a verb and its object ("Cancel booking", not "OK"). A button that says only 'OK' goes against it, so this is not built. "I want it this week" does not change the rule; changing DES-5 itself is a design decision for a person, as a new request.

key: IN-7623
title: "week view: hovering a booking shows who booked it"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-7623]
---

## Intent
Hovering a booking in week view shows who booked it, next to the time it already shows.

## Acceptance
- Given a booking by Ana Silva, when a team member hovers it in week view, then the tooltip shows the time and "Ana Silva".
- Given the public booking page, when a visitor sees taken times, then the name of another person is not shown.

## Boundaries
- Adds a field to the team view only; must not show names on the public booking page.

Allowed by AUT-1 (new fields that add to what is there and take nothing away).

key: IN-8160
title: "settings page: typo 'Calender' → 'Calendar'"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:product]
sources: [IN-8160]
---

## Intent
Fix the typo 'Calender' on the settings page to 'Calendar'.

## Acceptance
- Given the settings page, when it is shown, then it says 'Calendar' and nowhere 'Calender'.
- Given any other page, when it is shown, then its copy is not changed.

## Boundaries
- Copy only; must not rename settings keys, API fields or export columns.

Allowed by AUT-1 (copy changes in the product's own interface).

key: IN-9594
title: "week view: 'today' button missing on phones"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-9594]
---

## Intent
The 'today' button shows in week view on phones, as it does on larger screens.

## Acceptance
- Given a phone 375 px wide, when week view opens, then the 'today' button is shown and jumps to the current week.
- Given a desktop screen, when week view opens, then the 'today' button is not moved or changed.

## Boundaries
- Must not change other controls of week view.
- Uses the spacing scale (DES-3); no new raw values.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

---
key: SCHED-4412
title: "colours: move hard-coded colours to design tokens"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:product]
---

## Intent
Move every hard-coded colour in components to the `--color-*` design tokens (DES-2). Nothing visible changes.

## Acceptance
- Given the component sources, when they are searched for raw hex, rgb() or named colours, then there are none; every colour is a `var(--color-*)` token.
- Given any page before and after the change, when it is rendered, then it looks the same (screenshot diff shows no change).
- Given a colour that has no token yet, when it is moved, then it is not given a new value: it maps to the nearest existing palette token, and the page does not change colour.

## Boundaries
- Must not add new colours or change any colour value in the tokens file.
- Must not change layout, type or copy.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bringing code in line with a rule in specs/ when nothing visible changes; DES-2).

---
key: SCHED-4418
title: "week view: first day of the week follows the account locale"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-3326]
---

## Intent
Week view starts on the first day of the week of the account locale, not always on Sunday.

## Acceptance
- Given an account with locale de-DE, like the Berlin studio in IN-3326, when week view opens, then the week starts on Monday.
- Given an account with locale en-US, when week view opens, then the week still starts on Sunday.
- Given a booking on any day, when the start day changes, then the booking is not moved and keeps its UTC time (PRD-2).

## Boundaries
- Must not change stored bookings, the calendar feed or exports.
- Uses the account locale only; no new setting.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes and small features inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

key: SCHED-4431
title: "booking page: show remaining seats"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:client]
---

## Intent
The booking page shows how many seats are left on group slots.

## Acceptance
- Given a slot with 8 seats and 5 bookings, when the booking page shows it, then it says 3 seats left.
- Given a slot with one seat, when the booking page shows it, then no seat count is shown.
- Given a full slot, when the booking page shows it, then it is not offered as bookable.

## Boundaries
- Adds a field; must not remove or rename anything on the booking page.
- Must not change how seats are counted or stored.

Allowed by AUT-1 (new columns, filters or fields that add to what is there and take nothing away).

key: SCHED-4446
title: "CSV export: times carry no UTC offset"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:analytics]
---

## Intent
The CSV export gets a UTC offset column next to the start and end times, so tools that read it know the zone (ADR-0001).

## Acceptance
- Given a booking at 09:00 Europe/Warsaw in winter, when it is exported, then the new offset column says +01:00.
- Given an existing export, when it is compared with the new one, then every old column is still there, with the same name, order and values (PRD-3).
- Given a client tool that reads the start and end columns, when it reads the new export, then those columns are not changed.

## Boundaries
- Must not change or remove existing columns (PRD-3).
- Must not change the date format of existing columns (see IN-1210, a person decides that).

Allowed by AUT-1 (new columns that add to what is there and take nothing away; bringing code in line with ADR-0001).

---
key: SCHED-4452
title: "calendar sync: Outlook events arrive twice"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
---

## Intent
Calendar sync pushes each booking to Outlook once, with a stable id, so Outlook shows it once (ADR-0002).

## Acceptance
- Given a booking synced to an Outlook calendar, when sync runs twice, then Outlook shows one event.
- Given a booking that changed, when sync runs, then the existing event is updated, not a second one created.
- Given an event edited in Outlook, when sync runs, then sched-prod does not read it back (ADR-0002, sync stays one-way).

## Boundaries
- Must not add reading from external calendars (ADR-0002).
- Must not change how all-day bookings go out in the calendar feed: midnight to midnight, as a client relies on it (IN-9975, AUT-2).

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

key: SCHED-4458
title: "invoice PDF shows net and gross"
status: done

Invoice PDFs list net, tax and gross on separate lines.

key: SCHED-4463
title: "type: move hard-coded font sizes to the type scale"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:product]
---

## Intent
Move every hard-coded font size in components to the type scale in the tokens (DES-1). Nothing visible changes.

## Acceptance
- Given the component sources, when they are searched for font sizes, then every one is a type-scale token.
- Given any page before and after the change, when it is rendered, then it looks the same.
- Given a size that is not on the scale, when it is moved, then no new step is added to the scale; it maps to the nearest existing step.

## Boundaries
- Must not add steps to the type scale or change its values.
- Must not change colours, spacing or copy.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bringing code in line with a rule in specs/ when nothing visible changes; DES-1).

---
key: SCHED-4465
title: "API: rate-limit replies carry no Retry-After header"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:client]
---

## Intent
API replies with status 429 carry a Retry-After header that says when to try again.

## Acceptance
- Given a caller over its rate limit, when the API answers 429, then the reply has Retry-After in seconds until the limit resets.
- Given a caller under its limit, when it calls the API, then the reply does not carry a Retry-After header.
- Given the change, when limits are compared before and after, then no limit value has changed.

## Boundaries
- Must not change rate-limit values, plans or anything about pricing (AUT-2).
- Adds a header only; must not change reply bodies.

Allowed by AUT-1 (small features inside the specs that add to what is there and take nothing away).

key: SCHED-4468
title: "spacing: move hard-coded margins to the spacing scale"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:product]
---

## Intent
Move every hard-coded margin and padding in components to the 4 px spacing scale in the tokens (DES-3). Nothing visible changes.

## Acceptance
- Given the component sources, when they are searched for margin and padding values, then every one is a spacing token.
- Given any page before and after the change, when it is rendered, then it looks the same.
- Given a value that is not on the 4 px scale, when it is moved, then no new step is added; it maps to the nearest step.

## Boundaries
- Must not add steps to the spacing scale or change its values.
- Must not change colours, type or copy.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bringing code in line with a rule in specs/ when nothing visible changes; DES-3).

key: SCHED-4486
title: "audit log: keep 90 days"
status: open
labels: [needs-human, from:finance]
---

## Question
Finance asks to keep audit log entries for 90 days and then delete them. Should stored audit entries be deleted, and from when?

## Options
1. Delete every entry older than 90 days, the ones already stored included, and keep deleting daily.
2. Apply the 90 days to new entries only; entries already stored stay until someone decides on them.
3. Do not delete: archive entries older than 90 days out of the live log.

## Recommendation
Option 2, after a person checks the client terms for how long audit data must be kept.

## Why
Because deleting data that is already stored needs a human (AUT-2), and an audit log may be part of what the client terms promise (AUT-2).

---
key: SCHED-4494
title: "week view: a booking across midnight shows on its first day only"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
---

## Intent
In week view, a booking that crosses midnight shows on both days it covers.

## Acceptance
- Given a booking from 23:00 to 01:00, when week view shows that week, then it shows on the first day until midnight and on the second day from midnight.
- Given an all-day booking stored as midnight to midnight, when week view shows it, then it shows on its one day only, not on the next day too.
- Given the calendar feed, when it is read after the change, then all-day bookings still go out as midnight to midnight.

## Boundaries
- Must not change how all-day bookings go out in the calendar feed: midnight to midnight, as a client relies on it (IN-9975, AUT-2).
- Must not split or change stored bookings (PRD-1); display only.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

key: SCHED-4498
title: "confirmation email: the cancel link opens the login page"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-5369]
---

## Intent
The cancel link in the booking confirmation email opens the booking without a login, as the cancel link in the reminder email already does.

## Acceptance
- Given a person who booked without an account, when they open the cancel link in the confirmation email, then they see their booking and can cancel it.
- Given the reminder email, when its cancel link is opened, then it still works as before.
- Given a cancel link for one booking, when it is opened, then it does not show or cancel any other booking.

## Boundaries
- Must not change how team members sign in.
- Use the same link mechanism as the reminder email; no new kind of token.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

skill.name: triage
skill.text:
---
name: triage
description: Use when requests for a product (support tickets, team chat, client mail, a backlog) must go into its issue tracker so that every open issue is either ready for an agent (agent-ready) or marked for a person (needs-human), with every request traced to an issue and every call cited to a rule id.
---

# triage: requests in, a marked tracker out

Input: the product's backlog, its request channels and its specs (rules with ids).
Output: a tracker where every request sits in the `sources` of exactly one issue, and every
open issue carries exactly one mark: `agent-ready` or `needs-human`.

The harness sorts. It never makes a call the specs give to a person.

## 1. Collect everything first

1. Read the specs whole: the autonomy rules (what an agent may do alone, what needs a person)
   and every product, design and decision rule. Note each rule's id.
2. Pull the backlog and every channel. Channels keep filling: poll with the cursor until
   several rounds in a row bring nothing new. Keep the raw replies; never triage from memory.
3. Make one table: request id, channel, who sent it, the text. Read them all before you
   decide any of them, because one request often changes another (a client's "leave it as it
   is" is a boundary on someone else's "change it").

## 2. Decide each request, in this order

For each request ask, and stop at the first yes:

| Question | Then |
| --- | --- |
| Did shipped work already answer it (a `done` issue, a request "from the old queue", "filed before the fix")? | `closed`, reason `obsolete`; cite the done key |
| Is it the same ask as an issue already in the tracker? | add the id to that issue's `sources` (or close as `duplicate`, `duplicate-of` set) |
| Does it go against a spec rule (a modal for errors, raw colour values, a lost export column, two-way sync)? | `closed`, reason `contradicts-spec`; cite the rule id |
| Does it ask for no work ("please leave X as it is")? | `closed`, reason `not-planned`; cite the request, and copy it as a boundary into every issue that could touch X |
| Does it hit a "needs a human" rule (a thing a client said they rely on, pricing/invoices/terms, deleting or rewriting stored data)? | open, `needs-human` |
| Does an "agent may do alone" rule cover it, line for line? | open, `agent-ready`; cite that rule id |
| None of the above (product scope, a new rule, a trade-off)? | open, `needs-human` |

Rules that decide close calls:

- **Urgency is not permission.** "URGENT", "before Friday", "one-line change" change nothing.
  Judge the change, not the tone.
- **A request that conflicts with another person's request is a person's call** — unless a
  spec already decides it, then cite the spec. Put both request ids in the `sources` of one
  `needs-human` issue whose question names both sides (a "leave it as it is" that collides with
  an open "change it" goes there, not into a separate `not-planned`).
- **A later request can withdraw an earlier one.** When the sender takes back their own ask
  ("forget the rename from earlier"), close the earlier issue as `obsolete` with both ids in
  its `sources`. This is why you read everything before you hand in.
- **Shape it to fit the rules before you send it up.** If a request can be met by a change the
  autonomy rules allow (built on the existing tokens, scales or palette; a new column instead
  of a changed one), write the agent-ready version and say so. Send it to a person only when no
  allowed shape exists.
- **Prerequisites are `blocked-by`.** If the rule an agent-ready issue rests on is not true in
  the code yet (raw values still in components, a migration still open), the issue is
  `blocked-by` the open issue that makes it true.
- **Backlog issues are triaged too.** Every open backlog issue gets a mark and a body in the
  right shape. `done` and `closed` ones keep their status.

## 3. Write the issue

Use the tracker's own format (the README names it). Keep the frontmatter fields: `key`,
`title`, `status`, `reason` (closed only), `labels` (one mark plus `from:<who>`), `sources`,
`blocked-by`, `duplicate-of`.

agent-ready, a brief an agent can ship from without asking:

```
## Intent
What changes, in a sentence or two.

## Acceptance
- Given …, when …, then …
- Given …, when …, then … not …   (at least one case of what must not happen)

## Boundaries
- Must not touch …   (copy in every client "leave it as it is" that applies)

Allowed by AUT-x (the autonomy rule id).
```

needs-human, a question a person can answer:

```
## Question
What has to be decided?

## Options
1. …
2. …

## Recommendation
Option …

## Why
Because … (the fact it rests on, by its id: rule, issue key or request id).
```

closed: one paragraph that says what decided it, with the rule id, issue key or request id.

## 4. Check before you hand it in

Run these as a script over the tracker files, not by eye:

- every request id from every channel appears in the `sources` of exactly one issue;
- every open issue has exactly one of `agent-ready` / `needs-human`;
- every agent-ready body has Intent, Acceptance (with a "not" case), Boundaries and an
  `Allowed by AUT-…` line;
- every needs-human body has Question, two or more Options, Recommendation and Why with an id;
- every closed issue has a `reason`, and `duplicate-of` when the reason is `duplicate`;
- every `blocked-by` and `duplicate-of` points at a key that exists.
- Poll the channels once more right before the hand-in; a late request is still a request.
